verdict.rationale: The API docs state that developers try the API in the Console playground and then generate API keys on the API keys page, so self-serve key minting is documented. Pricing is also published per model without sales contact. However, the evidence never documents the account sign-up flow, never explicitly rules out a waitlist or approval gate, and gives no step-by-step key-creation walkthrough beyond a one-line pointer. Missing for 10: documented self-serve account sign-up steps, explicit evidence of no waitlist or approval gating, a detailed step-by-step key-minting guide, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the onboarding flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can sign up and mint an API key self-serve — no sales call, no waitlist gymnastics — and the docs say exactly how

citations.quote: In the Console, you can use playground (platform.claude.com/playground) to try out the API in the browser and then generate API keys on the API keys page
Pricing docs publish per-MTok prices for every current model without sales contact
